The photo shows the plate spanning about 420 px along its diagonal, so about 16 px per cm. The corn is about 100 px wide, which is about 6 cm.

STEP 3 - Items: One corn cob segment, with no sauce or butter visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The corn is about 6 cm in diameter, so its area is about 28 cm^2. That is about 7% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: The segment is about 3 cm tall, but it is seen end-on, so the height is uncertain. Taking 3 cm gives 28 x 3 = 85 ml. The cob is round and tapered, so I use about 75 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: The corn is dense, with kernels on a cob core. A density of about 0.7 gives about 55 g. The cob is inedible, but the weight of the visible food includes it. I use 55 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Boiled corn on the cob is about 96 kcal/100 g for the kernels. Including the cob, the figure is closer to 90 kcal/100 g. 55 g x 0.9 = about 50 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A 3 cm slice of corn on the cob weighing about 55 g is plausible.
